title: Understanding and Detecting Fail-Slow Hardware Failure Bugs in Cloud Systems
problem: Hardware components in cloud systems can degrade gradually by becoming slow rather than failing completely, creating silent performance failures that are difficult to detect using traditional binary failure detection mechanisms.
motivation: Fail-slow hardware failures cause insidious performance degradation in cloud services, reducing reliability and quality of service without triggering standard alerting systems.
method: Empirically characterizes fail-slow failure behaviors through instrumentation and monitoring of cloud hardware. Develops detection algorithms that analyze system performance signals and hardware telemetry to identify gradual degradation patterns and predict fail-slow states.
key_novelty: Focuses on detecting and understanding fail-slow hardware failures that manifest as performance degradation rather than immediate component failure.
contributions: Characterization of fail-slow hardware failure modes and their signatures in cloud systems
Detection system and algorithms for identifying fail-slow failures in production
Analysis of failure propagation and impact on workload performance
Evaluation demonstrating effectiveness on real cloud infrastructure
limitations: Specific limitations not discussed in title.
primary_theme: Detecting gradual hardware degradation in cloud systems
